title: Author spec file conforming to openSUSE guidelines and macro conventions
input: Create an openSUSE spec file for a system daemon. What openSUSE-specific macros should be used for CMake building, systemd scriptlets, and test execution?
evidence_requirements: Use of %ctest for test execution in %check section

title: Diagnose Open Build Service build failure using osc CLI
input: An OBS package shows status `failed` for repository `openSUSE_Tumbleweed` on `x86_64`. How does an engineer investigate the failure from the command line?
evidence_requirements: Checking build status using osc results
Fetching the remote build log using osc buildlog or osc log
Locating the compiler error or unpackaged files warning in the log output

title: Configure multi-distribution targets in Open Build Service project
input: An openSUSE package maintainer wants their OBS home project to build packages simultaneously for openSUSE Tumbleweed, openSUSE Leap 15.6, and Fedora 40. How is this configured in OBS?
evidence_requirements: Editing project metadata using osc meta prj -e
Adding <repository> definitions linking to openSUSE:Factory, openSUSE:Leap:15.6, and Fedora:40

title: Execute complete osc package development and submit request workflow
input: A maintainer wants to update a package in `openSUSE:Factory`. What is the complete sequence of `osc` commands from branching to creating the final submit request?
evidence_requirements: Branching the package via osc branch openSUSE:Factory <package>
Checking out and testing locally via osc co and osc build
Committing changes and creating a submit request via osc commit and osc sr

title: Enforce openSUSE Shared Library Policy on package naming
input: A project builds `libxyz.so.2.1.0` with SONAME `libxyz.so.2`. According to openSUSE Packaging Guidelines, what MUST the binary package containing the library be named?
evidence_requirements: Naming the package strictly libxyz2 matching the SONAME
Separating development symlinks and headers into libxyz-devel
Explanation that this enables parallel installation of different library major versions

title: Reconcile spec file differences between Tumbleweed and openSUSE Leap
input: Tumbleweed uses GCC 14 and modern Python 3.12, while Leap 15.6 has GCC 12 and Python 3.6/3.11 modules. How should an openSUSE spec file handle toolchain differences across both targets?
evidence_requirements: Use of conditional macros testing 0%{?suse_version} and 0%{?is_opensuse}
Checking suse_version > 1500 for Tumbleweed vs <= 1500 for Leap
Conditionally requesting newer compiler packages or Python stacks for Leap
